To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
earnings reported under IAS 39 are generally more timely than earnings reported using IFRS before the convergence, and that the timeliness has deteriorated after a series of convergence in China.

earnings reported under the Chinese accounting standards (pre-convergence with International Financial Reporting Standards) have a lower earnings recognition timeliness (earnings response coefficient) and a higher future earnings recognition timeliness compared to earnings reported under International Financial Reporting Standards.

the earnings response coefficient of Chinese GAAP earnings decreased after the first harmonization and convergence in 2006 and that the future earnings coefficient of Chinese GAAS earnings increased after the second harmonization and convergence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of a harmonization and convergence process with IFRS, which is the most important international standard, on the timeliness in the recognition of earnings in an emerging economy.
the timeliness of the recognition of earnings reported in emerging capital markets.
the effect of harmonization and conversion with IFRS of Chinese accounting standards on the timeliness in recognition of earnings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

convergence of national accounting standards with international accounting standards may be a necessary condition for improving the quality of accounting information, but is not a sufficient condition.
harmonization and convergence may not necessarily lead to higher accounting quality in the emerging Chinese capital markets.

the timeliness and quality of recognition of earnings under Chinese GAAP is not necessarily better than the timeliness and the quality of recognition of IFRS earnings before Chinese GAAP converges with IFRS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the convergence of IFRS and Chinese GAAP does not necessarily lead to the convergence of accounting quality.

harmonization with IFRS may have a positive impact on earnings quality for developed markets but a negative impact on earnings quality of emerging markets, which may be due to a lack of enforcement of IFRS in the latter.
Chinese accounting standards are not as good as IFRS, but the Chinese accounting standards are getting better over the time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
accounting standard setters in emerging capital markets should be aware of the possibility of a decrease in accounting quality when harmonizing and convergencing with IFRS.

the timeliness and relevance of earnings reported under national accounting standards in emerging capital markets are likely to be improved through the adoption and enforcement of high-quality auditing standards.
the quality of accounting standards is not a necessary condition for the quality of accounting information.
